# models.energetics { #wdm.models.energetics }

`models.energetics`

Energy expenditure: resting metabolism, the thermic effect of food, and
adaptive thermogenesis.

Total daily energy expenditure is decomposed as

$$
E(t) = \underbrace{c_0 + c_1 W(t)}_{\text{resting + baseline activity}}
+ \underbrace{\mathrm{TEF}(t)}_{\text{cost of digestion}}
+ \underbrace{X(t)}_{\text{logged exercise}}
+ \underbrace{A(t)}_{\text{adaptation, } \le 0}
$$

The first three terms are algebraic functions of the current state and input.
The fourth is a *state* with its own dynamics, because adaptation lags changes
in intake by roughly a fortnight -- and that lag is the only thing that makes it
even partially distinguishable from a simple error in $c_0$.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [adaptation_rate](#wdm.models.energetics.adaptation_rate) | Time derivative of adaptive thermogenesis, kcal/day per day. |
| [baseline_expenditure](#wdm.models.energetics.baseline_expenditure) | Expenditure *excluding* adaptive thermogenesis, kcal/day. |
| [effective_intake](#wdm.models.energetics.effective_intake) | Metabolisable energy intake for the day, kcal/day. |
| [thermic_effect](#wdm.models.energetics.thermic_effect) | Energy spent digesting and processing the day's food, kcal/day. |
| [total_expenditure](#wdm.models.energetics.total_expenditure) | Total daily energy expenditure, kcal/day, including adaptation. |

### adaptation_rate { #wdm.models.energetics.adaptation_rate }

```python
models.energetics.adaptation_rate(x, u, p, carb_ref_g)
```

Time derivative of adaptive thermogenesis, kcal/day per day.

First-order relaxation toward a target proportional to the prevailing energy
gap:

$$
\dot A = \frac{-\beta_A D - A}{\tau_A},
\qquad D = E_{\text{base}} - I
$$

A sustained deficit $D > 0$ drives $A \to -\beta_A D$, lowering
expenditure and shrinking the effective deficit. Loss therefore decelerates
toward a new equilibrium even at constant intake -- the plateau, as a
two-line differential equation rather than a moral failing.

### baseline_expenditure { #wdm.models.energetics.baseline_expenditure }

```python
models.energetics.baseline_expenditure(x, u, p, carb_ref_g)
```

Expenditure *excluding* adaptive thermogenesis, kcal/day.

Separated out because it is the reference against which the energy gap
driving adaptation is measured. Using total expenditure there instead would
make the adaptation dynamics implicitly self-referential.

### effective_intake { #wdm.models.energetics.effective_intake }

```python
models.energetics.effective_intake(x, u, p, carb_ref_g)
```

Metabolisable energy intake for the day, kcal/day.

On days with a food log this is simply the logged (fiber-corrected) value.
On days without one it is set to the subject's *current* total expenditure,
which is the neutral assumption: absent evidence, predict no net energy
imbalance rather than inventing a deficit or a surplus.

This is an approximation, and a slightly optimistic one in a specific sense
-- unlogged days are, empirically, more often high-intake days than low ones.
The corresponding process-noise inflation in `wdm.models.dynamics`
widens the uncertainty on such days but does not correct that bias.

### thermic_effect { #wdm.models.energetics.thermic_effect }

```python
models.energetics.thermic_effect(u, carb_ref_g)
```

Energy spent digesting and processing the day's food, kcal/day.

Protein costs 20-30 % of its own energy to process, carbohydrate 5-10 %, and
fat almost nothing. The practical consequence is that isocaloric diets are
not metabolically equivalent: shifting 100 g of carbohydrate to protein
raises expenditure by roughly ``(0.25 - 0.075) * 400 = 70`` kcal/day at
identical total intake.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                                           | Default    |
|------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| u          | DailyInput | The day's inputs. ``carb_dev_g`` is a deviation from the reference (habitual) intake, so the absolute carbohydrate intake is recovered by adding back ``carb_ref_g``. | _required_ |
| carb_ref_g | float      | Reference (habitual) carbohydrate intake, g/day; the episode mean only when no habitual reference is given.                                                           | _required_ |

#### Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

Falls back to a fixed fraction of total intake when the macro split is
missing, which keeps the term continuous across days with partial logs
rather than introducing a spurious jump.

### total_expenditure { #wdm.models.energetics.total_expenditure }

```python
models.energetics.total_expenditure(x, u, p, carb_ref_g)
```

Total daily energy expenditure, kcal/day, including adaptation.
